title: Launch shape = cloud-signup-first: Brainiac's MVP is a hosted product a stranger signs up for, not a self-hosted deploy
body: Decided during the /mvp launch-readiness run (2026-08-05). The first market release is a cloud signup funnel into the console, not a docker-compose README. Consequences accepted: the prod domain, auth lifecycle, and signup->activation analytics become P2/P3 launch-gating work, while DEPLOY.md self-host stays supported but is no longer the primary onboarding path. The three killer features must each be reachable from a fresh cloud account with no local Postgres.

title: Value case cut to 3 killer features: permission-aware retrieval inside the vector scan, provenance + review gate, contradiction adjudication + temporal validity
body: Decided during the /mvp launch-readiness run (2026-08-05). (1) RLS-enforced permission-aware retrieval INSIDE the vector scan - the row filter is applied by Postgres RLS during the ANN scan, not as a post-filter, so an agent can never be served memory its project cannot see. (2) Provenance + review gate - every served memory carries where it came from and nothing reaches the org corpus without passing review. (3) Contradiction adjudication + temporal validity - the store finds memories that disagree, adjudicates them, and knows which one is currently true. Everything else in the product (skills library, demand loop, KB publishing, console modules) is supporting cast for the launch narrative and must not compete for landing-page or onboarding real estate.

title: Monetization = free during beta, one project per Google account, with an explicit revisit trigger
body: Decided during the /mvp launch-readiness run (2026-08-05). No pricing page, no billing dependency, no plan/tier table for the MVP. The quota that makes 'free' bounded is one project per Google account. Revisit trigger: when either (a) a single account asks for a second project, or (b) hosted infrastructure cost stops being absorbable at the current signup rate - whichever comes first. Recording the decision (rather than deferring it) is what closes the P0 monetization item; the revisit trigger is what keeps it honest.

title: P1 rails wired for the launch push: context map re-swept by subtree, feature inventory and KPI pass run through the Personas bridge, memory outbox seeded
body: The /mvp P1 rails item (path A) was executed on 2026-08-05. The pre-existing context map was a single 2026-07-23 whole-repo scan: 25 contexts, 0 groups, 258 of ~420 source files. It was re-swept subtree-by-subtree (crates / console / migrations) per the project-populate doctrine, then the feature-inventory and KPI lanes were run against the refreshed map. This file is the launch journal surface the item requires; every later /mvp session should append its decisions here rather than to a scratch doc.

title: The Personas dev-tools bridge lives on 17400-17415 - :17320 is the test-automation server and answers /health, which reads like the bridge being up
body: Cost a false premise in the 2026-08-05 /mvp run: an assessor verified 'the loopback bridge is UP' with curl 127.0.0.1:17320/health, which returned {"status":"ok","server":"personas-test-automation"}. That is a DIFFERENT server. The scan/KPI/context bridge that project-populate drives takes the first free port at or above 17400 and exposes /dev-tools/* - probe with: for p in $(seq 17400 17415); do curl -s -m 1 http://127.0.0.1:$p/dev-tools/projects >/dev/null && echo $p && break; done. Neither server exposes a Ship-milestone route; milestones are Tauri IPC commands (dev_tools_create_milestone / dev_tools_create_goal / dev_tools_set_milestone_item) reachable only by evaluating JS in the app webview via the test-automation /eval endpoint.
